title: Google, Phirsty Life and PhirstMaxx: your steps

intro.verdict_html:
Version 2, 2026-11-23 late. Your ticks and answers from version 1 are kept: the step numbers are unchanged, and the new steps are added on the end of their phase.

Done tonight: the Google app is published, the redirect list is tight, Kirsty's Google account exists, Phirsty Life is created, the five old May-era calendars are deleted, and the Google secrets are rotated (rotation guide). The reconnect broke twice and is fixed: router prefetches replaced the sign-in check (Claude Code, commit 3e611a2), then the allowlist was missing on Vercel.

Decided tonight: the shared calendar is Phirsty Life, permanently, shared only with Kirsty. Friends in your Google, Apple and Spotify family groups are kept out of everything about the two of you. Mycelium reads your other calendars through the Google connection; the secret iCal feeds are retired.

cells: Only Google accounts you list as test users
Any Google account, for its own calendar only; Mycelium then refuses every account except pwhelanonline@gmail.com
Until you revoke it, or six months unused
Only accounts inside a Google Workspace organisation
Needs a paid Workspace. Not offered to a personal Gmail.

prerequisites: Signed in to Google as pwhelanonline@gmail.com
Kirsty's inbox (you hold it until handover)
cost: Phase 4 puts a card on file but stays at £0 with the caps in 4.4

phases.title: Publish the Google app and lock it down
phases.lede_html: Order that works: publish (1.3), put GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS on Vercel and redeploy (6.2), then reconnect (1.4). A reconnect before either of those is wasted.

steps.title: Find the right project

where.label: Google Cloud → Google Auth Platform → Clients

steps.body_html: The client Mycelium uses is mycelium: it is the one with the redirect address below, and its Last used date moves when you reconnect. Type the project name (top bar) in the box. mycelium-calendar-agent was the May 2026 email-to-calendar experiment; delete it if its Last used date is May.

blocks.label: The redirect address to look for

steps.title: Trim the redirect addresses
steps.body_html: Keep exactly the production address below; Authorised JavaScript origins empty. As of 2026-11-23 that is already the state, so there is nothing to save. Add http://localhost:3000/api/google/callback only if you ever want to connect for real from a local build.

notes.html: Google delivers a sign-in code only to an address on this list. With your own domain as the only entry, a code for this app cannot be sent anywhere else. Leave Use this client for an AI-powered agent unticked.

steps.title: Publish the app

where.label: Google Auth Platform → Audience → Publishing status

steps.body_html: Publish app → Confirm; the status reads In production. Done 2026-11-23. Ignore any prompt to submit for verification.

notes.html: Publishing stops the weekly token expiry. It does not let anyone into Mycelium or your calendar: Mycelium's login guards the button, and the allowlist refuses every Google account except yours.

steps.title: Reconnect, after publishing and after the allowlist is live
steps.body_html: First check 6.2's GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS is on Vercel (Production) and a deploy newer than commit 3e611a2 shows Ready. Then press CONNECT or RECONNECT once, in one tab, choose pwhelanonline@gmail.com, and on Google hasn't verified this app press Advanced → Go to … (unsafe) → Continue. You land back on Integrations with a notice; type it in the box.

notes.html: The notices: Reconnected as … is success. That Google account isn't allowed here means the wrong account was picked or the running deploy lacks the allowlist. Sign-in expired, try again means ten minutes passed. bad_state should no longer appear; if it does, tell Claude Code (it was the router prefetching CONNECT, fixed in 3e611a2).

steps.title: Name the one Google account Mycelium may accept
steps.body_html: Your Google address. It is the whole value of GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS, and Kirsty's address is never added to it: her Mycelium login does not connect Google.

verify_html: Audience shows Publishing status: In production.
Settings → Integrations shows Google connected as your address.
myaccount.google.com/connections lists the app with Google Calendar access and nothing else.
Eight days from now it is still connected. The daily health check messages you if it is not.
phases.why_html: A Google sign-in is one person's grant to one app for that person's own data. Publishing widens who may give a grant; it never hands anyone your data. The sign-in check (a nonce in a cookie, compared on the way back) stops a forged return link attaching someone else's account; the allowlist stops any account but yours being stored at all.

phases.title: Kirsty's account and the Phirsty Life calendar
phases.lede_html: The shared calendar is Phirsty Life, not "Family": your Google and Apple family groups each have their own auto-made calendar, your friends are in those groups, and a second calendar of the same name invites a wrong tap. Phirsty Life is permanent; Mycelium syncs with it rather than replacing it.

steps.title: Create Kirsty's Google account
steps.body_html: Done 2026-11-23. You hold the inbox and set her up yourself until handover (phase 8). This address is also her Mycelium login.

notes.html: Until phase 8 you can read her email. Phase 8 hands every key back: her own password, 2-Step Verification on her phone, her recovery details, and your sessions signed out.

steps.title: Add the account to her Android phone

where.label: Kirsty's phone → Settings → Passwords & accounts → Add account → Google

steps.body_html: Deferred to handover. When you do it: sign in with her address, leave Calendar sync on, open Google Calendar and tick Phirsty Life. Her email can stay in Outlook.

steps.title: Create the shared calendar in your account

where.label: Google Calendar → Settings → Add calendar → Create new calendar

steps.body_html: Done 2026-11-23 as Phirsty Life, signed in as {{google_account}}. Check its time zone in its settings reads (GMT+00:00) United Kingdom Time.

steps.title: Share it to Kirsty with edit rights, and nobody else

where.label: Google Calendar → Settings → Phirsty Life → Share with specific people or groups

steps.body_html: Add people and groups → her address → permission Make changes to events → Send. Then read the list: it must show Kirsty and nobody else. Leave Make available to public unticked.

notes.html: Not Make changes and manage sharing: that would let the calendar be shared onward from her side. Mycelium checks this list too: it refuses to use a calendar anyone else can see, and stops writing if someone is added later.

steps.title: Accept the invite from her inbox

where.label: Gmail as kirstykjpetco@gmail.com → the email from Google Calendar

steps.body_html: Open the invite and press Add this calendar. Until someone does, it does not appear on her side.

steps.title: Show it on your iPhone
steps.body_html: Apple Calendar: tick Phirsty Life, Save, then Calendar app → Calendars → tick it under your Google account. Google Calendar app: menu (☰) → tick it.

steps.title: Copy the calendar's ID

where.label: Google Calendar → Settings → Phirsty Life → Integrate calendar

steps.body_html: Copy Calendar ID (ends @group.calendar.google.com) into the box. It is an address, not a secret. Do not copy the Secret address in iCal format: that one is a password and nothing needs it.

steps.title: Keep the family group calendars out of it

where.label: Google Calendar → left column → Premium Calendar; iPhone → Calendar → Calendars

steps.body_html: The Google family group's calendar is renamed Premium Calendar (any group member can rename it back). Untick it in Google Calendar and on the iPhone so it never shows in a picker. Do the same with Apple Family Sharing's own Family calendar (Calendar → Calendars). Never put anything about you and Kirsty in either, and do not add Kirsty to those groups.

notes.html: Your friends can read, edit and re-share the family group calendars. The May experiment had put four Amazon orders, with your village, into the Google one.

steps.title: Clear out the old calendars

where.label: Google Calendar → Settings → each calendar → Remove calendar

steps.body_html: Done 2026-11-23: Events, Fitness, Finance, Travel and Sporebit deleted (empty or stale since the May experiment); Birthdays was already gone. Left: Personal, Phirsty Life, Holidays in United Kingdom, and the hidden Premium Calendar. Mycelium now reads Personal through the Google connection, not a secret iCal feed.

verify_html: Phirsty Life's sharing list shows Kirsty only.
An event added on her side shows on your iPhone within a minute, and moving it on your phone moves hers.
Premium Calendar and Apple's Family calendar are unticked on your iPhone.
phases.why_html: Google shares calendars one at a time, so edit rights on Phirsty Life say nothing about your other calendars. Both phones talk straight to Google, which is why it works before Mycelium is involved; Mycelium then becomes a third reader and writer of the same calendar. A Mycelium-hosted .ics subscription was rejected: phones could only read it, Google refreshes subscriptions only a few times a day, and the link is a bearer secret.

phases.title: Free keys: routing and YouTube
phases.lede_html: Neither needs a card. Keep each key in its tab or your password manager until phase 6, never in a chat.

steps.title: OpenRouteService key
steps.body_html: Create the account (a HeiGIT account), confirm the email, sign in. The dashboard shows a free Standard key; if none, request a free token named Mycelium. Free plan: 2,000 route requests a day, 40 a minute, non-commercial use.

notes.html: The key goes into phase 6 and nowhere else.

steps.title: Turn on the YouTube Data API

where.label: Google Cloud → APIs & Services → Library → YouTube Data API v3

steps.body_html: Same project as phase 1 ({{gcp_project}}). Press Enable. No billing account needed.

steps.title: Create a key that can only call YouTube
steps.body_html: Create credentials → API key. API restrictions → Restrict key → tick only YouTube Data API v3. Application restrictions: None (Vercel has no fixed address). Save and copy.

notes.html: It reads public YouTube data only, and the restriction makes a leaked copy useless for anything else.

verify_html: The OpenRouteService dashboard lists one Standard key.
Credentials lists Mycelium YouTube with one API under Restrictions.
Both are tested for real in 6.3.
phases.why_html: PhirstMaxx needs door-to-door times (OpenRouteService: driving, walking, cycling from open map data) and a video's title, description and location tags to work out which place it is about (YouTube's own API, no scraping).

phases.title: Google Maps key (optional, needs a card)
phases.lede_html: Only for real public-transport times and Google's place details. Recommended tonight: answer 4.1 with later and tick the rest. PhirstMaxx works without it.

steps.title: Decide: now or later
steps.body_html: Each Maps product has a free monthly allowance (10,000 basic, 5,000 Pro, 1,000 Enterprise calls). The key needs a billing account, which needs a card.

steps.title: Add a billing account
steps.body_html: Country United Kingdom, your card, linked to {{gcp_project}}. Google may place a small temporary hold.

steps.title: Enable the two APIs

where.label: Google Cloud → APIs & Services → Library → Routes API

steps.body_html: Enable on Routes API, then on Places API (New). Nothing else.

steps.title: Cap it so the bill cannot leave £0
steps.body_html: Every per-day request quota on both APIs: 30 (at most 930 a month, under the smallest free allowance). Then Budgets & alerts: a £1 budget with alerts at 50% and 100%. Mycelium also stops itself at 900 calls a month per product. As it turned out (2026-11-24): Google marks the per-day quotas not adjustable, so the 900-a-month counter in Mycelium is the hard stop; the £1 budget alerts at 50/90/100/150%; the billing account is a free trial ending in about 90 days, after which Google refuses and both readers fall to the free route.

notes.html: A budget only emails you. The quota is the hard stop.

steps.title: Create a key that can only call those two
steps.body_html: Create credentials → API key → Restrict key → tick Routes API and Places API (New) only. Save and copy.

verify_html: If now: Routes API and Places API (New) enabled, 30 a day on each, the £1 budget listed.
If later: 4.1 says later and the rest is ticked.
phases.why_html: A hard daily cap that adds up to less than the smallest free allowance means the charge cannot exceed nothing, whatever the app does; Mycelium's own counter is a second stop.

phases.title: The old PhirstMaxxing database address (skipped: no old data wanted)
phases.lede_html: The importer reads the live old app so PhirstMaxx starts with your real blocks, plans and ideas. PC only.

steps.title: Copy the connection string
steps.body_html:
Skipped 2026-11-24 (Phil): no old data is wanted. The old Supabase project is being deleted, PHIRSTMAXX_OLD_DB_URL is not needed, the importer is never run against it, and PhirstMaxx starts empty. Removing the old app (Vercel project, IONOS DNS record, PWA on both phones) is MYC-211.

Pick PhirstMaxxing, not Mycelium. Connect → Session pooler → copy the URI (it holds [YOUR-PASSWORD]).

steps.title: Put the database password in

where.label: Supabase → Database → Settings → Reset database password

steps.body_html:
Skipped 2026-11-24 (Phil): no old data is wanted. The old Supabase project is being deleted, PHIRSTMAXX_OLD_DB_URL is not needed, the importer is never run against it, and PhirstMaxx starts empty. Removing the old app (Vercel project, IONOS DNS record, PWA on both phones) is MYC-211.

If you don't have it, reset it to letters and digits only and save it in your password manager. The old app keeps working (it uses API keys). Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with it.

notes.html: Full access to the old database. .env.local on the PC only: not Vercel, not this page, not a chat.

verify_html: Starts postgresql://postgres., contains pooler.supabase.com:5432, no square brackets.
6.3 reads a row count through it.
phases.why_html: The session pooler works from a home connection without IPv6, and keeping the address on the PC means the most powerful secret here never leaves your machine.

phases.title: Put the values where Mycelium reads them
phases.lede_html: If pasting multi-line or long values into Vercel is fiddly, Claude Code can copy them from .env.local with the Vercel CLI without printing them (prompt in 6.2).

steps.title: The PC: .env.local
steps.body_html: Add the lines below (values straight after =, no quotes). Skip GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY if 4.1 says later. No old-database address: phase 5 is skipped. GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS may already be there from Claude Code.

steps.title: Production: Vercel
steps.body_html: GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS is already on Production (2026-11-23). Add the keys below with Environment Production and Sensitive ticked, never the old database address. Or paste the prompt to Claude Code. Values only reach the live site after a redeploy.

blocks.label: Or: prompt for Claude Code
blocks.text: Add ORS_API_KEY, YOUTUBE_API_KEY and (if present) GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY to Vercel Production from .env.local, marked sensitive, with vercel env add. Confirm GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS is there. Never print a value, only names and added / already there. Do not add PHIRSTMAXX_OLD_DB_URL. Redeploy production and report when Ready.

steps.title: Test all three from the PC
steps.body_html: Each command reads its value from .env.local; nothing secret is typed or shown. Run them one at a time. The old-database check is gone with phase 5.

blocks.label: Routing: expect a distance near 66,000 metres and a duration near 3,300 seconds (Doncaster to York; the address is HeiGIT's api.heigit.org since the old api.openrouteservice.org was switched off in November 2026)
YouTube: expect Me at the zoo

shells.bash:
cd /a/Projects/Mycelium
k=$(grep -E '^YOUTUBE_API_KEY=' .env.local | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s "https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/videos?part=snippet&id=jNQXAC9IVRw&key=$k" | grep -o '"title": "[^"]*"' | head -1

blocks.label: Google Maps: expect a route of about 67 km and a place called High Force Waterfall (two calls, each one of the month's 900)

shells.bash:
cd /a/Projects/Mycelium
g=$(grep -E '^GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=' .env.local | cut -d= -f2-)
curl -s -X POST https://routes.googleapis.com/directions/v2:computeRoutes -H "X-Goog-Api-Key: $g" -H 'X-Goog-FieldMask: routes.duration,routes.distanceMeters' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"origin":{"location":{"latLng":{"latitude":53.5228,"longitude":-1.1285}}},"destination":{"location":{"latLng":{"latitude":53.96,"longitude":-1.0873}}},"travelMode":"DRIVE"}'
curl -s -X POST https://places.googleapis.com/v1/places:searchText -H "X-Goog-Api-Key: $g" -H 'X-Goog-FieldMask: places.displayName,places.formattedAddress' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"textQuery":"High Force Waterfall","regionCode":"GB","pageSize":1}'

verify_html: The routing command prints a distance and a duration.
The YouTube command prints a video title.
The database command prints a count.
Vercel lists the names under Production.
phases.why_html: .env.local is what the PC worker, the importer and local builds read; Vercel's variables are what production reads, and only from the next deploy on. Each place gets only the secrets it uses.

phases.title: Hand back to Claude Code

steps.title: Set the research spend
steps.body_html: Each drop's web research is one paid cloud AI call, a few pence. Inside the existing £5 monthly cap is fine to start.

fields.label: Research spend
fields.placeholder: inside the £5 cap / £3 a month of its own

steps.title: Paste this to Claude Code
steps.body_html: Fills itself in from the boxes above. Anything still in angle brackets is a box you have not filled.

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.text:
My steps for the Google, Phirsty Life and PhirstMaxx setup are done. Re-read claude/family-calendar-spec.md (merge the Claude project's 2026-11-23 amendments D2 and D7 to D10 with your as-built notes; never overwrite either side) and claude/phirstmaxx-spec.md, then build the family calendar sync and PhirstMaxx in the order I gave you.

Ship docs/checklists/google-family-phirstmaxx-setup.json in-app at version 2 (the calendar is "Phirsty Life"; new steps 2.8, 2.9 and phase 8 handover), start its run and set these answers, every step ticked except phase 8 and anything marked missing:
- Google Cloud project: {{gcp_project}}. Publishing status: {{publish_status}}. Client in use: mycelium.
- Reconnect notice: {{reconnect_notice}}. GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS={{google_account}} on Vercel and in .env.local.
- Shared calendar: "Phirsty Life", ID {{family_calendar_id}}, shared to kirstykjpetco@gmail.com with Make changes to events and nobody else; accepted. The Google family group calendar ("Premium Calendar") and Apple's Family calendar are never read or written.
- ORS_API_KEY and YOUTUBE_API_KEY are in .env.local and on Vercel.
- Google Maps key: {{maps_choice}}.
- PHIRSTMAXX_OLD_DB_URL is in .env.local only.
- Research spend: {{research_cap}}.

The family calendar picker must apply the ACL guard (refuse any calendar shared beyond me and Kirsty). Kirsty's Mycelium login is kirstykjpetco@gmail.com; she never connects Google. Do not stop for any of the above. Check each env name is present before relying on it and stop only for what is missing.

verify_html: Claude Code reports it has merged the spec and started on the family calendar.
It does not ask again for anything listed in the prompt.
phases.why_html: Claude Code cannot see this page, so the answers travel in the prompt and it writes them into the in-app copy of this checklist, where they stay.

phases.title: Handover to Kirsty (later)
phases.lede_html: When you give her the account. Until then you hold her inbox; this phase hands every key back so you cannot read her email afterwards.

steps.title: Her phone and her Google security

where.label: myaccount.google.com, signed in as Kirsty, on her phone

steps.body_html: With her: she changes the password, turns on 2-Step Verification with her own phone, sets her own recovery phone and email, and signs out every device that is not hers under Your devices. Then do 2.2 on her phone.

steps.title: Reset her Mycelium first run
steps.body_html: So she agrees to what is shared herself and enrols her own authenticator.

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.text: Handover to Kirsty: reset kirstykjpetco@gmail.com's Mycelium onboarding state so she does the partner first run herself, including confirming what is shared. Remove any authenticator or passkey I enrolled on her account, clear anything I created while testing as her (list it first), and send me her invite or first-run link to give her. Never print a secret.

steps.title: She checks what she sees
steps.body_html: Phirsty Life shows in her Google Calendar; none of your other calendars do. In Mycelium she sees the family space and only Day log entries you marked Shared.

verify_html: You can no longer sign in to her Google account.
Her Mycelium account asks her, not you, for its second factor.
phases.why_html: Holding a partner's inbox is a setup convenience, not an arrangement to keep. Handing over the password, second factor and recovery details together is what actually makes the account hers.

troubleshooting.cause: Before 3e611a2, the router prefetched CONNECT and replaced the sign-in cookie
troubleshooting.fix: Fixed in 3e611a2; if it comes back, tell Claude Code.

troubleshooting.symptom: That Google account isn't allowed here
troubleshooting.cause: The wrong account was picked, or the running deploy predates GOOGLE_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS
troubleshooting.fix: Pick pwhelanonline@gmail.com; check 6.2 and redeploy with the build cache off.

troubleshooting.cause: The app is back in Testing
The production address is missing from the client

troubleshooting.symptom: Reconnect needed comes back after a week
troubleshooting.cause: The last reconnect was made while the app was still in Testing
troubleshooting.fix: Check 1.3 says In production, then 1.4 again.

troubleshooting.symptom: Mycelium refuses Phirsty Life in the picker
troubleshooting.cause: Its sharing list holds someone besides you and Kirsty
The invite was not accepted, or it is unticked in her app
troubleshooting.fix: 2.5; if the email is missing, remove her in 2.4 and add her again.

troubleshooting.symptom: Phirsty Life missing from Apple Calendar
troubleshooting.fix: 2.6, then pull to refresh in Calendars.

troubleshooting.symptom: A PowerShell paste does nothing or opens VS Code
troubleshooting.cause: Multi-line pastes can run line by line; a bare .js path opens in VS Code
troubleshooting.fix: Save scripts with notepad, then run them with node from A:\Projects\Mycelium.

troubleshooting.symptom: The YouTube test says the key is not valid
troubleshooting.cause: API enabled in a different project from the key, or wrong restriction
Unconfirmed email, or a space or line break in the key
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the email, re-copy the key, fix the line.

troubleshooting.cause: Placeholder still in the address, or the password has @ : / or #
PostgreSQL's folder is not on PATH
